g1_title: Why my open rate is falling
g1_intro: A falling open rate is rarely caused by a single factor. This guide helps you diagnose the 8 most common issues — from technical reputation to list fatigue — with a direct Neria solution for each one.
g1_tip: Benchmark: a healthy open rate in B2C e-commerce is between 18% and 28%. Below 15%, diagnosis is urgent. Above 35%, you're in the top tier.
g1_c1_t: Symptom: sudden drop with no changes on your end
g1_c1_b: Your IP or domain has been added to a blacklist (RBL). Recipients' mail servers silently reject your emails or redirect them to spam before they are even displayed. This is the most severe and often invisible cause.
g1_c1_f: Check your reputation score (42 RBLs verified) and configure SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
g1_c2_t: Symptom: emails land in spam, very low open rate
g1_c2_b: Certain words or formats (all caps, excessive punctuation, keywords like "FREE", "URGENT") trigger spam filters before the email is even opened. The message lands in the spam folder and is never read.
g1_c2_f: Analyse your subject line before each send — Neria detects 200+ problematic patterns and calculates a deliverability score.
g1_c3_t: Symptom: low rates for certain languages or countries
g1_c3_b: Sending at 3am to your Japanese customers, or at lunchtime when your UK customers are away from their desks, mechanically lowers open rates. Inbox competition is at its peak at the wrong moments.
g1_c3_f: Best windows: luxury e-commerce Tue–Thu 10–11am or 7–8pm · international customers: adapt to time zones · reactivation: Tuesday or Wednesday morning.
g1_c4_t: Symptom: emails arrive but are not opened
g1_c4_b: "noreply@luxury-house.com" suggests a machine, not a relationship. Recipients only open emails from people or brands they recognise and trust. The sender name is the first thing they see — before the subject line.
g1_c4_f: Use a human name tied to your brand, adapted by language ("Sophie at La Maison Luxe" for EN, "Sophie chez La Maison Luxe" for FR).
g1_c5_t: Symptom: the email preview shows "View this email in a browser…"
g1_c5_b: Preview text is the 2nd visible element in the inbox list. If absent, the email client displays the first text from the HTML — often an unsubscribe link or code — which damages your image and hurts open rates.
g1_c5_f: Write a preview text that complements (not repeats) the subject line. Neria injects it automatically in every template via the {preview_text} variable.
g1_c6_t: Symptom: gradual decline over several weeks or months
g1_c6_b: If you send the same type of email to the same audience too often, recipients become desensitised and stop engaging. This is natural and becomes irreversible beyond a certain threshold. The Ghost segment starts to grow.
g1_c6_f: Reduce send frequency, exclude ghosts from your campaigns, vary content. Neria's cooldown system prevents over-solicitation automatically.
g1_c7_t: Symptom: all your emails have a similarly poor rate
g1_c7_b: Sending the same message to your ambassadors (regular buyers) and your ghosts (inactive for 6 months) dilutes relevance. Each segment has its own motivations and responds to different messages.
g1_c7_f: Use Neria's 5 behavioural segments (Ambassador, Active, At-risk, Dormant, Ghost) to target each send. The impact is immediate.
g1_c8_t: Symptom: low open rates despite well-crafted subject lines
g1_c8_b: Without SPF, your domain can be spoofed. Without DKIM, your emails carry no cryptographic signature. Without DMARC, you have no domain protection policy. These 3 DNS records are non-negotiable to land in the primary inbox.
g1_c8_f: The reputation score tab generates the exact DNS records to copy-paste at your hosting provider or domain registrar.
g1_final: Best practice: audit these 8 points once a month. Most email modules on the market offer no diagnostic tools — Neria centralises them all in the Statistics tab.
g2_title: Writing a subject line that performs
g2_intro: The email subject line is the most important decision you make with every send. It is read in 2 seconds, on mobile, among 40 competing emails. These 5 rules come from analysing millions of e-commerce emails.
g2_tip: Reminder: Neria automatically analyses your subject line in the Deliverability score tab and alerts you before sending if issues are detected.
g2_r1_b: Beyond 50 characters, the subject line is cut off on most mobile devices. Below 20 characters, the hook is too vague. The sweet spot: 35–45 characters. Tip: count the first name length if you personalise.
g2_r2_b: The reader doesn't care what you're doing — they care what they're getting. "Order confirmation #45789" describes your internal process. "Your order is on its way ✈" speaks to your customer. Flip the sentence: what they get, not what you're sending.
g2_r3_t: Personalise with the first name — +26% open rate
g2_r3_b: Studies consistently show: a first name in the subject line increases open rates by 20–30%. Place it at the start ("Sarah, your order…") or at the end ("…just for you, Sarah"). Avoid the middle where it disrupts reading. Neria injects {firstname} automatically in all templates.
g2_r4_b: Curiosity ("What you don't know yet about your order"), real urgency ("expires tonight"), exclusivity ("reserved for our customers") — these emotions are legitimate. Fake urgency destroys long-term trust and ultimately lowers open rates across your entire list.
g2_r5_t: Test before deciding — that's what A/B Test is for
g2_r5_b: Your instincts are hypotheses, not certainties. Create two subject line variants, let Neria measure for 24–48h, then apply the winner to the rest of your base. A single A/B Test session can reveal differences of 8 to 15 open rate points.
g2_ex2_b: SPECIAL OFFER — URGENT — CLICK HERE NOW!!!
g2_ex2_a: Reserved for our customers: 20% off until Sunday
g2_ex3_a: Your order is on its way ✈, Sarah
g2_ex5_b: Have you thought about leaving a review?
g2_ex5_a: Sarah, your opinion means a lot to us ✦

g2_ex6_r: Focused on you, not the customer
g2_spam_h: Words and formats to avoid in subject lines
g2_spam_intro: These patterns trigger spam filters. Neria detects them automatically in the deliverability score:
g2_warn: Watch out for caps: more than 40% of the subject line in capitals triggers filters on Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail. A single capitalised word for emphasis is generally tolerated — not an entire phrase.
g2_emoji: Emojis: a well-placed emoji can increase open rates by 5–10%. Rule: 1 emoji maximum, at the start or end of the subject, consistent with the message. Avoid emoji strings (🎁🎁🎁🔥🔥) which signal spam.
g3_intro: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies to all your emails, whether transactional or marketing. This guide summarises your concrete obligations and explains what Neria handles automatically — and what remains your responsibility.
g3_warn: Important: this guide is for information only. For your specific situation, consult a lawyer or your DPO. GDPR penalties can reach 4% of global annual turnover or €20M.
g3_legal_h: The 3 legal bases for your emails
g3_lc3_items: Must always include an unsubscribe link
Can be challenged if the customer objects
g3_o1_title: Unsubscribe link — mandatory in every marketing email
g3_o1_body: The GDPR requires a simple, free means of withdrawing consent in every marketing communication. The absence of this link exposes you to direct penalties.
g3_o1_items: Neria automatically includes the link in all templates (footer)
The /neria/unsubscribe endpoint processes and records unsubscribes immediately
The List-Unsubscribe header is automatically added (Gmail/Outlook compatibility)
g3_o2_body: Any request to unsubscribe, correct or delete data must be processed within 30 calendar days. The UK ICO and EU authorities recommend aiming for 10 working days.
g3_o2_items: Neria unsubscribes are immediate and timestamped
The customer is blacklisted: no marketing email will be sent to them
Complete data deletion is handled from the GDPR tab
g3_o3_title: Right to erasure — data deletion on request
g3_o3_body: When a customer requests data deletion, this includes email history, tracking data, custom variables and logs. Simply unsubscribing is not enough to fulfil an erasure request.
g3_o3_items: Table-level purge available in the GDPR tab
Sensitive data is AES-256 encrypted at rest (even in the event of a breach)
g3_o4_title: Data retention — 3 years recommended by data protection authorities
g3_o4_body: Data protection authorities recommend not retaining data from inactive prospects or customers beyond 3 years after the last contact or purchase. Beyond that, anonymise or delete.
g3_o4_items: The Ghost segment (inactive 12+ months) is your primary indicator to monitor
Configure data retention in the GDPR tab
Schedule regular purges — at least once a year
g3_cl_note: Tick each item as you go. Your responses are saved locally in your browser.
g3_ch1_l: Functioning unsubscribe link in all your marketing emails
g3_ch1_n: Neria includes it automatically — verify it hasn't been removed from a custom template.
g3_ch2_l: Documented consent for every email address on your list
g3_ch2_n: Date, source and collection method. Without proof, consent has no legal standing.
g3_ch3_l: Up-to-date privacy policy mentioning email marketing
g3_ch3_n: It must describe the purposes, retention period and rights of individuals.
g3_ch4_n: GDPR tab → Data retention. Recommended: 3 years after the last purchase.
g3_ch5_l: AES-256 encryption of sensitive data enabled
g3_ch5_n: GDPR tab → Encryption section. Rendered data is encrypted at rest.
g3_ch6_n: Illegal without explicit consent from listed contacts. Risk of spam complaints + GDPR fines.
g3_ch7_n: Segmentation tab → Ghosts. More than 3 years without a purchase: anonymise or delete.
g3_ch8_n: The GDPR tab calculates an automatic score based on 3 axes (unsubscribe, retention, PII).
g3_final: What Neria handles automatically: unsubscribe link, List-Unsubscribe header, AES-256 encryption, configurable retention, table-level purge, and GDPR report with A–F score. Your role: document consent, train your team, keep your privacy policy up to date.
